To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the genomic responses to ovariectomy in aged rats were different from those induced by dietary Ca restriction.

the genomic responses in the tibial metaphysis of ovariectomised rats to dietary Ca deficiency were distinct from those in the same tissue of Ca-deficient rats, and that the genomic responses to Ca deficiency were mediated by the expression of carbonic an hydrase II.
the genomic responses in proximal tibias of aged rats to ovariectomies and dietary Ca deficiency are different.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the differential mRNA expression profiles in bone in response to ovarian hormone deficiency and dietary Ca deficiency.
the genomic response to ovariectomization and low-Ca diets in aged rats.
the differential mRNA expression profiles of bone tissue in proximal tibias of aged rats in ovariectomy and Ca deficiency models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ovariectomised animal is a better model than dietary Ca deficiency for investigating the genomic responses of aged bone to osteoporosis.

both ovariectomy and Ca deficiency induced bone loss in proximal tibial metaphysis of aged rats through distinct mechanisms, and the combination of ovariectomy and LCD induced the additive effect on bone loss in aged rats.
ovariectomy induces bone loss through an increase in osteoclastic activity, whereas low-Ca diet induces bone loss through the induction of osteoclastogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ovariectomy and Ca deficiency induce bone loss in aged rats via different molecular mechanisms.
ovariectomised rats and rats fed with a low-Ca diet are two distinct models for osteoporosis.
ovariectomy and Ca-deficient diet induce different genomic responses in the proximal metaphysis of aged female rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genomic responses to ovariectomy are different from those to dietary Ca deficiency.
the bone loss induced by dietary Ca deficiency and ovariectomy are differentially mediated by different genes.
the genomic responses to ovariectomy or dietary Ca deficiency are different, and the genomic responses to the two different models of bone loss should be investigated in separate studies.
